methods.notes: Service UUID is the primary matcher. The local name is an additional hint, not a reason to select another Artiphon model.

identification.notes: Filter on the standard BLE-MIDI service. The advertised and post-connection names can differ, so the name alone is not sufficient.

device.name: Artiphon Orba 2
device.notes: Handheld instrument and looper. Performance uses standard MIDI/BLE-MIDI; configuration uses the proprietary SysEx command layer declared here. Both work locally without an Artiphon account. Only one BLE central may connect at a time. Never blind-scan registers: invalid reads can fault and reboot the instrument. Erase and fresh-record commands are marked advanced because they destroy recorded material.

openness.notes: Artiphon did not publish a third-party protocol specification. The cited community specification reports byte-identical checks against captured BLE traffic and a live Orba 2. This YAML restates its wire facts without copying its implementation.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the other central, then reconnect.

pairing.notes: The public client connects directly without a PIN or application account. The one-central limit is a connection limit, not bonding.

credentials.notes: No credentials are required for local MIDI or SysEx control.

factory_reset.description: No factory-reset procedure is asserted by the cited protocol source. Do not use erase-song as a device reset.
factory_reset.effect: Not established: whether settings, pairings or recordings are cleared is undocumented. Erase-song deletes recorded material only and is not a device reset.

methods.description: Connect by the BLE-MIDI service UUID, subscribe to the MIDI I/O characteristic, then send documented SysEx commands in order.
methods.name: BLE-MIDI connection

steps.action: Wake the Orba 2 and close every other app connected to it.
Connect to the peripheral advertising the BLE-MIDI service.
Send only documented commands, serializing all writes belonging to one SysEx message.

setup.notes: Wake the Orba, close any other central, connect and enable MIDI notifications. No account or cloud setup is needed.

rejoin.notes: BLE-only. Close the previous central and reconnect.

testing.notes: Not driven by this project. The framing, registers and command values below consolidate holofermes/orba-protocol's public capture-verified specification. Orba 2 only: Orba 1, Orba 3, Chorda and INSTRUMENT 1 are not claimed compatible. The bundled vectors come from that public specification and are independently rebuilt by scripts/test_artiphon_orba_2_spec.py.

initialization.notes: MIDI I/O; reassemble SysEx replies through F7 before decoding.

OrbaCommandPacket.description: Unwrapped command or reply before the LSB-first 8-to-7-bit encoding.
parse_rules: Bytes 0-1 are 82 01; byte 2 correlates the reply; bytes 3-4 are the payload length u16 BE.
The final two bytes are CRC-16 BE, reflected polynomial A001 with initial zero, over byte 0 through the final payload byte.
Payload 02 = GET and 03 = SET, followed by a domain and a u16 BE register address.
Only read documented addresses: invalid register reads can reboot the device.

protocol_details.fx_addressing: Domain 02, register high byte 50. Part bases are Lead 00, Chord 08, Bass 10 and Drum 18. Offsets are volume +0, pan +1, reverb +2 and delay +3. Every FX SET requires the trailing 00 01 04; without it the device can acknowledge the write but not apply it. Preset changes reset that part's FX. The four volume commands above cover every part; the pan, reverb and delay examples show the same rule for other clients.
protocol_details.reply_handling: A reply is not necessarily one GATT notification. Reassemble BLE-MIDI through F7, remove header/timestamp bytes, undo the 7-bit packing and verify length and CRC before using the payload. MIDI clock is not supported. Preset filenames, battery response semantics and the exact metronome enum need further work before being presented as typed state.

remaining_unknowns: Orba 1, Orba 3, Chorda and INSTRUMENT 1 are not proven compatible.
Preset selection requires a 129-byte filename and a separate commit; filenames are not enumerated here.
Metronome's exact value vocabulary needs a capture.
The app-level response schemas are intentionally limited to documented request/response framing; unknown register semantics stay opaque.

erase_active_loop.description: Erase only the active part's loop.

fresh_record.advanced_reason: Wipes the existing loop before recording.
fresh_record.description: Erase the existing loop and arm a fresh recording.

get_battery.description: Request the battery register; decode the SysEx reply.

set_active_part.description: Select Lead, Chord, Bass or Drum.

set_tempo.description: Set tempo; the UI displays BPM and the wire carries BPM x100.

transport_pause.description: Pause playback while preserving the loop.

transport_record_overdub.description: Record or overdub without erasing the existing loop.

framing.notes: The command template is the Orba payload (GET/SET, domain, address, values), NOT a complete SysEx. Wrap it as 82 01 <id> <payload-length:u16be> <payload> <crc:u16be>; CRC-16 uses reflected polynomial A001, initial zero, over 82 through the final payload byte. LSB-first 8-to-7-bit pack that packet, prefix 00, and delimit with F0/F7. BLE-MIDI first writes are 80 80 <up to 18 stream bytes>, continuations are 80 <up to 19 bytes>, and the final write is 80 80 F7. The message id is the command's serial parameter (zero for a one-shot command).

characteristics.name: MIDI I/O and Orba SysEx control
characteristics.notes: Standard MIDI performance and Orba control share this characteristic. Incoming BLE-MIDI packets need stateful reassembly through F7; do not interpret each notification as a complete SysEx reply.
